requirements.evidence: All contract pieces are present: migrations with cascading FKs, the unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16,26-27); Queue/Ticket models with the required fillable, casts and relations; enums; InactiveQueueException; IssueTicket with negative-priority check (IssueTicket.php:27-29), a lockForUpdate re-read of the queue (:46-50) and a 5-attempt retry on UniqueConstraintViolationException (:31-39). nextCode orders by id and skips malformed codes (Ticket.php:81-104). The write-once updating hook is at Ticket.php:40-49, and call() checks membership, locks and checks the status (:113-136). The factory store() override allocates codes at insert time (TicketFactory.php:46-55). Two small gaps: the retry only works when the action runs in its own top-level transaction, and the collision retry has no test, so it is unverified.

conventions.evidence: IssueTicket lives in app/Actions as an invokable class, $fillable is set deliberately, both migrations have down(), and docs/business-rules.md and docs/database-schema.md are updated. Deviations: Ticket::call authorizes with an inline membership check (Ticket.php:118-120) instead of a policy or gate, which goes against 'Authorization always goes through policies/gates'. CHANGELOG.md:17 copies the new entry into the already released [0.0.0] section, which breaks Keep a Changelog. The database-schema.md 'Ticket write-once' note was left saying only called_at and called_by_user_id are mutable, but status is mutable too.

security.evidence: Membership is checked server-side before any write and the ticket is left unchanged when the check fails (Ticket.php:116-120; test at TicketIssuance:157-167). Fillable lists are explicit and exclude called_by_user_id/called_at (Ticket.php:16). Status is re-read under a row lock to prevent a double call (:124-128). The only weakness is that authorization bypasses the policy layer. It works, but it is not centralized.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TicketIssuanceTest.php covers: the defaults; per-queue sequences; inactive and stale-inactive queues with nothing persisted (:48-62); negative priority; A999 to A1000 to A1001; no reuse after delete; malformed codes; factory forQueue; the unique constraint; immutability of code and priority; single call; a stale double call; a non-member call; and cascade. Missing: no test exercises the collision retry, and the test titled 'deleting a queue or its entity cascades' (:169-176) only deletes the entity.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall. nextCode pages backwards in batches of 100 with a do/while and 'break 2' (Ticket.php:84-102), which is more machinery than a straightforward query needs. It is justified by the malformed-code skipping rule, but it is still somewhat elaborate. The factory store() override is minimal.

readability.evidence: Clear names (MUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUANCE, CODE_PREFIX, MAX_ATTEMPTS), useful comments on the lock/staleness reasoning (IssueTicket.php:51-52, Ticket.php:122-123) and PHPDoc @throws on public methods. The infinite 'for ($attempt = 1; ; $attempt++)' loop (IssueTicket.php:31) is slightly unusual but readable.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, enums, exception, action, factories, migrations, docs and tests. There is no UI, totem API or call-next logic, and the only Entity change is the queues() relation (Entity.php:41-44).

issues.explanation: The new entry is duplicated into the released [0.0.0] section; it belongs only under [Unreleased].

The member-only call rule is enforced with an inline membership check and a hand-thrown AuthorizationException rather than a policy or gate, which goes against the project's 'authorization always through policies' rule.
The retry on a (queue_id, code) collision, which the task requires, has no test exercising it.
If the action is called inside an outer transaction, DB::transaction becomes a savepoint; on PostgreSQL the failed insert can poison the outer transaction, so the retry would not help.
The test is named 'deleting a queue or its entity cascades' but only deletes the entity; a direct queue deletion is not tested.
The existing write-once note still lists only called_at/called_by_user_id as mutable and omits status, which contradicts the new note added at line 606.
The batched backwards scan with 'break 2' is more elaborate than needed; a simpler formulation would be easier to follow.

review.summary: The change adds queues and tickets with migrations, models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action (row-locked active check, collision retry) and a write-once, member-only single call, with docs and a broad Pest test suite. The core requirements are met correctly. Remaining issues are small: the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated into a released version, authorization bypasses the policy layer, and the collision retry is untested. Approvable with minor fixes.
